title: This Fish Has Clear Blood and No Red Cells. How Does It Live?
subject: Antarctic icefish

scenes.text: This fish has blood as clear as water. It should be dead.
Antarctic icefish are the only vertebrates with no hemoglobin. Sixteen species, out of about fifty thousand.
No hemoglobin means no red blood cells. Their blood is transparent.
So how do they breathe? They soak up oxygen straight from the water, through gills and skin.
The Southern Ocean is freezing, and cold water holds more oxygen. That's the whole secret.
Which is why they can't live in warm water. Take away the cold, and the trick stops working.

description:
This fish has blood as clear as water.
Antarctic icefish are the only vertebrates that lack hemoglobin. They survive by absorbing oxygen from the cold Southern Ocean through their gills and skin.
Would you trade red blood for the cold?
first_comment: Whalers noticed these fish had no red blood around 1900. What other animal should we dig into next?
